quotes.name: Coen Cartier
quotes.quote: When the system runs light on a weekend, the bus feels different — you notice the regulars more. The folks who ride every day, they're still there, but there's no rush. You get a chance to actually say hello, maybe ask how someone's day is going. Riders don't see that part. They just see the bus showing up. But for us, it's the difference between moving a crowd and moving people. And on a quiet day, you see the city itself more — the light on the buildings, the empty sidewalks. It's a slower rhythm, but it's still a rhythm.

quotes.name: Evan Lewis
quotes.quote: When the system runs light on a weekend, you feel it in your bones before you ever see the numbers. 12th Street is the heart of downtown — that's where people transfer, where they catch the game or head to an event. When it's quiet there, it's not just empty platforms. It's the whole city catching its breath. I see it on my route too — fewer folks waiting, more empty seats, and a kind of stillness that tells you everyone's home or somewhere else entirely. The construction around the Baylight District doesn't help either; when streets get torn up, people just find another way, even if the bus still runs on time.

interviews.name: Evan Lewis
interviews.quote: When the system runs light on a weekend, you feel it in your bones before you ever see the numbers. 12th Street is the heart of downtown — that's where people transfer, where they catch the game or head to an event. When it's quiet there, it's not just empty platforms. It's the whole city catching its breath. I see it on my route too — fewer folks waiting, more empty seats, and a kind of stillness that tells you everyone's home or somewhere else entirely. The construction around the Baylight District doesn't help either; when streets get torn up, people just find another way, even if the bus still runs on time.
